sections.title: Describing a Celebration
sections.content: Everything from this unit comes together to describe a celebration: the party words, tener for age, the date pattern, and the action verbs — all in the same few sentences you'd use to tell a friend about a birthday.

items.spanish: Todos cantan y decoran la casa.
items.english: Everyone sings and decorates the house.

sections.content: 'La *celebración*' is feminine, like most Spanish nouns ending in -ción — the same pattern as 'la tradición'.

sections.title: Saber: to know (a fact, or how to)
sections.content: You already know conocer, for knowing a person or place. saber is different: use it for facts and information, and with an infinitive for knowing how to do something. The reading uses it already: 'Meg no sabe que sus amigos preparan una sorpresa.'

items.spanish: Meg no sabe que sus amigos preparan una sorpresa.
items.english: Meg doesn't know that her friends are planning a surprise.
Carlos knows how to sing very well.
Do you know how to dance?

items.spanish: No sé cocinar, pero sé decorar una fiesta.
items.english: I don't know how to cook, but I know how to decorate a party.

sections.content: yo sé is irregular — not 'sabo'. Everything else follows the regular -er pattern: sabes, sabe, sabemos, saben.
